A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAD-Flower and retain the same core formulation, algorithm, theorem and original experiments. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Internal inconsistencies in v3 are identifiable reporting issues rather than missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on Maze2d, Hopper, Walker2d and Kuka Block-Stacking, including baseline comparisons and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds Adroit Relocate evaluations, additional comparator results, model-error experiments and computation measurements.

M1.justification: The main flow-matching model, delayed activation and CBF/CLF quadratic program remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 introduces an uncertainty-dependent robust barrier condition and modified controller, described as an SOCP. This adds a robustness variant, although conflicting descriptions of it as implemented and hypothetical leave its experimental use unclear.

E1.justification: v3 adds D4RL Adroit Relocate, extending evaluation to contact-rich dexterous manipulation with 39-dimensional states and 30-dimensional actions. Original navigation, locomotion and stacking coverage remains; Medium locomotion results move to Table 8. Appendix J discusses physical deployment but reports no real-robot evaluation.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates rejection sampling across the original tasks and CoBL-Diffusion on Maze2d Large in Appendix D, substantially expanding constraint-handling comparisons. The original six baselines and DPCC-T/C/R comparisons remain. Applying the original comparator set to Adroit is an extension of coverage, not another comparator addition.

E3.justification: New protocols vary constraint strength, forward-model training-data fractions and injected dynamics noise. Additionally, v1 Appendix E specifies Maze2d actions in [-0.1, 0.1], whereas v3 Appendix F specifies [-0.9, 0.9]. This is a substantive reported setting revision, but v3 Section 6.1 retains the old bound, preventing an unambiguous account of which setting produced the revised results.

E4.justification: v3 adds constraint-strength sensitivity (Table 6), forward-model data-size robustness (Table 7), Gaussian dynamics-noise examples (Table 11), and broader computational analysis (Table 20). Section 6.3 also reports a CBF-only ablation, without a separate quantitative display. Original activation-time, integration-step and constraint-tightening analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report values with ± spreads without defining those spreads or specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. New tables retain the same reporting practice; changed spread values are result changes.

E6.justification: v3 adds Adroit, comparator, robustness and runtime results. It also revises existing Maze2d entries: SAD-Flower's Large reward changes from 1.42±0.52 to 1.69±0.26, and Diffuser's admissibility violation from 0.89±0.01 to 0.09±0.01. These cannot establish same-setting improvements because action bounds changed inconsistently. Moreover, v3 Tables 13–14 retain SAD-Flower's older Large reward.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.4 adds Lemma B.3 and its proof bounding accumulated state error under learned dynamics, followed by a proposed robust barrier/controller formulation. v3 also changes the SDF gradient norm from 1/2 to 1 and replaces determinant conditions in Theorem B.2 with rank conditions and corresponding proof edits. The central Theorem 5.1 is retained.

C1.justification: The central claims of guaranteed constrained planning through control-augmented flow matching without retraining remain. The introduction adds an explicit claim of scalability to dexterous grasping and high-dimensional robotic systems. The abstract and conclusion otherwise preserve their principal scientific claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and limitation discussions: it distinguishes learned-model consistency from true-system consistency, identifies failures under severe model mismatch, and discusses extension to other ODE samplers. Appendix J addresses planning versus real-time control, computational costs, sensing and perception-dependent constraints, explicitly leaving physical deployment to future work.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the default c=0.5, reward-model training and Monte Carlo candidate selection for the FM planner, and broader runtime measurements. Existing architecture, training and hardware tables are retained. The standalone code-release promise and base-code URL disappear, while a video/demo project link is added; the PDFs do not establish an actual code release.

R1.justification: v3 expands positioning through a new capability-comparison table, more explicit distinctions from CoBL, and discussion of SAD-Flower as a general ODE-sampling control layer. It adds substantial supporting literature on robust CBFs, model-error bounds, simulator fidelity and efficient robotic deployment. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: The original section sequence and much of the exposition remain. v3 makes targeted introductory and experimental rewrites, reorganizes feasibility discussion into numbered remarks, updates authorship and headings, and changes end matter. The reproducibility statement, appendix contents list and LLM-use statement are removed; these edits do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column main text with a two-column conference layout, separates Algorithm 1 from Figure 1, splits the original performance table, transposes the main DPCC table, and rearranges Figure 4 into a two-by-two display. Numerous new tables and the dynamics-noise trajectory panel substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: New model-error tests, dexterous manipulation results, comparators and deployment limitations strengthen empirical assessment. However, Appendix B.4's printed robust barrier condition subtracts an uncertainty margin, weakening the original condition rather than establishing its claimed safety guarantee; its implementation status is also contradictory. Conflicting Maze2d bounds and main-versus-appendix rewards further weaken interpretability. These useful additions coexist with material theoretical and reporting problems, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
